title: Methodology for hydraulic characterisation of the sand filter backwashing processes used in micro irrigation
author: de Deus, Mesquita, et al.

steps.title: Assemble experimental circuit
steps.instruction: Construct the closed‑loop water circulation system as shown in Fig. 2, including a 50 m³ municipal‑water tank, a centrifugal pump (Meganorm Bloc, KSB, nominal flow 100 m³ h⁻¹, rotor 332 mm, 25 cv, 1760 rpm, 60 Hz), two needle valves (one upstream and one downstream of the sand filter), the selected sand filter (F1‑Hidro Solo, F2‑Marbella or F3‑Amanco) fitted with tempered‑glass side panels for visualisation, the electromagnetic flow sensor (Signet 2551, Georg Fischer) and ultrasonic flow sensor (UFM170, FMS), two MPX5700DP pressure transducers with integral pressure sensors, and the NI PCI‑6221 data‑acquisition board running LabVIEW.

substeps.instruction: Obtain the manufacturer’s technical specifications for the chosen sand filter: filter diameter, filtration surface area, inlet and outlet pipe internal diameters, useful height (distance from diffuser plate base to upper drain level), number of drains, average drain opening width, number of openings per drain, opening area per drain unit, total drainage area, and drainage‑to‑filter‑area ratio.
Mount the tempered‑glass side viewers on the steel‑sheet filter housing to allow visual measurement of bed expansion.

steps.title: Install and locate sensors
steps.instruction: Mount the flow sensors and pressure transducers according to ASABE 1993 recommendations: place each sensor at least 50 × the pipe internal diameter downstream of the preceding valve and at least 5 × the pipe internal diameter downstream of the sensor itself.

substeps.instruction: Electromagnetic sensor range: pipe diameter 12.7–304.8 mm, flow 0.05–10 m s⁻¹, accuracy ±0.5 %, temperature ‑10 to 70 °C, max pressure 1030 kPa at 25 °C.
Ultrasonic sensor range: pipe diameter 12.7–7620 mm, flow ‑16 to 16 m s⁻¹, accuracy ±0.5 %.
Pressure transducer range: 15–700 kPa, supply 4.75–5.25 V, max current 10 mA, accuracy ±2.5 %, response 1 ms, operating temperature ‑40 to 125 °C, transfer function P(kPa)=155.54·Vout(V)‑31.11.

steps.title: Prepare sand media
steps.instruction: Select silica sand of the desired particle‑size class and fill the filter to the prescribed bed height.

substeps.instruction: Particle‑size classes: G1 0.5–1.0 mm (CU = 1.50), G2 0.8–1.2 mm (CU = 1.27), G3 1.0–1.5 mm (CU = 1.34). Determine size distribution according to ABNT EB‑2097 (1990).

Define three bed heights (H1, H2, H3) as equal fractions of the filter’s useful height (Hi) that can be fluidised (see Table 1). Ensure the static layer allows a minimum expansion of 25 % of its height (Brouckaert 2004).

steps.title: Calculate target surface velocity
steps.instruction: For each test, compute the required flow rate (Q) that yields the desired surface velocity (vₛ) using Q = vₛ × A, where A is the filter cross‑sectional area.

substeps.instruction: Reference surface velocity: 0.01 m s⁻¹ (Pizarro Cabello 1996).
Define extreme velocities equally spaced above and below 0.01 m s⁻¹; the maximum velocities observed in de Deus et al. (2020) were 0.07 m s⁻¹ for F1, 0.045 m s⁻¹ for F2, and 0.044 m s⁻¹ for F3.

steps.title: Run backwash test (empty filter)
steps.instruction: Perform backwash runs with the sand filter empty to assess the pressure‑loss contribution of the equipment alone.

substeps.instruction: Set the pump to deliver the calculated flow rate for the chosen surface velocity.
Open the upstream needle valve, close the downstream valve, then open the downstream valve to start upward flow.
Run the backwash for 180 s; use the first 80 s for system stabilisation and record data for the subsequent 100 s.
Record inlet and outlet pressures at ~1 Hz (average one data point per second) via the NI PCI‑6221 system.
Repeat each surface‑velocity condition three times for each of the three filters (3 filters × 9 velocities × 3 reps = 81 runs).

steps.title: Run backwash test (filled filter)
steps.instruction: Repeat the backwash procedure with the filter packed with the selected sand media and bed height.

substeps.instruction: Set the pump to the same flow rate as calculated for the target surface velocity.
Start the upward flow as in the empty‑filter test and maintain it for 180 s, recording pressures for the stabilised 100 s interval.
Visually measure the expanded bed height (H₀) immediately after the 180 s run using the side glass panels.
Repeat each combination of filter (F1‑F3), sand size (G1‑G3), bed height (H1‑H3), and surface velocity (9 levels) three times (3 × 3 × 3 × 9 × 3 = 729 runs).

steps.title: Calculate pressure loss and expansion
steps.instruction: Process the recorded data to obtain pressure loss (ΔP) and bed‑expansion percentage.

substeps.instruction: ΔP = P_inlet − P_outlet for each run.
For filled‑filter runs, compute the media‑only pressure loss by subtracting the corresponding empty‑filter ΔP at the same surface velocity.
Calculate expansion percentage E using E = (H₀ − H) / H × 100, where H is the static bed height (H1, H2 or H3).

steps.title: Determine minimum fluidisation velocity
steps.instruction: Identify the surface velocity at which the pressure‑loss curve of the media‑filled filter intersects the linear pressure‑loss curve of the empty filter.

substeps.instruction: Plot ΔP versus surface velocity for each experimental combination.

Locate the intersection point (minimum fluidisation velocity) where the curve changes from linear increase to a plateau, following the methodology of Burt (2010) and the theory of Gupta & Sathiyamoorthy (1999).

steps.title: Document and analyse results
steps.instruction: Compile all measured and calculated values, including flow rates, surface velocities, pressure losses, expanded heights, expansion percentages, and minimum fluidisation velocities for each filter‑sand‑height combination.
